correctness.rationale: The explicit real unbounded diagonal D has compact resolvent; bounded self-adjoint rank-one and compact antisymmetric perturbations give a self-adjoint nonpositive compact-resolvent generator. The positive reference semigroup has simple zero eigenvalue with spectral gap. The exact reducing-subspace formula yields an antisymmetric entry -h_n(t)/2. Dyson–Phillips ordered-integral estimates give the nonnegative reference off-diagonal entry at most n²exp(-3n²)(exp(2t)-1). Taylor and elementary exponential inequalities prove the negative correction dominates whenever t>0, n>=ceil(t+3). A separate uniform-tail bound h_n(t)/u_n→0 and Duhamel estimate prove eventual strong positivity of each nonzero positive orbit. The identity at t=0 is positive. Standalone script verified rational numerical constants and sanity checks, while the all-real-time infinite-dimensional quantifiers are proved analytically. Source premises were independently reconstructed.

value.rationale: The all-time positivity-time set {0} is a qualitative extremal classification, stronger than failure at an unbounded set of integer times. It locates the maximal separation between individually eventually strongly positive orbits and absence of even one positive operator within the natural self-adjoint compact-resolvent real Hilbert-lattice class central to the motivating 2026 question. The explicit coordinate cutoff explains the mechanism. Earlier C(K) nowhere-positive examples are expressly acknowledged, so significance is claimed for the Hilbert self-adjoint realization and exact same-operator all-time result, not for the abstract phenomenon.
